info.bio:
Face to Face es una banda de punk rock formada en 1991 en Victorvill, California. Su nombre original era "Zero Tolerance". Ha estado desde sus comienzos ligada a la discográfica Fat Wreck.

En el 2004 la banda separó, y sus miembros se enrolaron en otros proyectos como: Me First and the Gimme Gimmes, The Offspring y Saves the Day. 

En 2008 se reunieron para tocar, y desde entonces han dado varios conciertos, incluso han anunciado el lanzamiento de un nuevo Lp para el año 2011.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Mid-90s Attention
podcast.body: Face to Face gained attention during the mid-1990s punk rock revival, performing "okay" in terms of record sales, though not reaching the massive numbers of the era's biggest bands. "Other punk bands to get attention during the middle 90s included Face to Face."

podcast.title: Success Following The Offspring
podcast.body: This band was discovered by fans due to The Offspring's significant success in late 1994, marking the beginning of Skate Punk's "glory years." "And this led to fans discovering bands like Goldfinger, Lagwagon, Face to Face, MXPX, and Unwritten Law."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Altercation with Patrick Carney of The Black Keys
xref.body: On September 13, 2015, Jack White ran into Patrick Carney of The Black Keys at a New York City bar called Cabin Down Below. Carney, who had never met White in person, claimed White tried to fight him, calling White a "40-year-old bully" and saying he inspired Carney to play music as a reaction against such "A-holes." White responded on Twitter, denying any physical altercation, stating he merely asked a question that Carney couldn't answer, and urged him to "speak face to face like a human being." "Patrick, I've never met Jack White until last night. He came to a bar in New York City, I go to a lot with a few friends and tried to fight me."

xref.title: Warped Tour Feature
xref.body: Goldfinger was one of the bands featured during the initial years of the Warped Tour, a key platform for pop punk and ska punk music. "In just the first few years, the tour featured bad religion, dancehall crashes, face to face, bucket nine, less than Jake, muddy, muddy boss tones, no doubt, sublime, and gold finger."
